title: Reverse percentages: what was the price before the sale?
examples: A jacket is 80 after 20% off. What was the original price?
How do you find the price before a discount?

explain.say: In a shop in São Paulo, a jacket costs 80 reais after 20 percent off. What was the price before? Many people add 20 percent of 80 and say 96. Let us see if that is right.

explain.say: The original price is the whole bar, 5 equal parts. Each part is 20 percent. The sale took one part away. So 80 reais fills the 4 shaded parts. That is 80 percent.
If 4 parts are 80 reais, one part is 80 divided by 4. That is 20 reais. See the one shaded part? Can you guess the whole price now?
All 5 parts are 5 times 20, which is 100 reais. That was the price before the sale! Quick way: divide by the multiplier. 80 divided by 0.8 is 100.

Well done! Look at the last bar: 96 is wrong, because 20 percent of 80 is smaller than 20 percent of 100. Wow: shops use this to remove tax from prices. Challenge: after a 10 percent rise a price is 110. What was it before?

faq.q: Why is the sale price 80 percent?
faq.a: The original is 100 percent, and 20 percent is taken off. 100 minus 20 leaves 80 percent.

faq.q: How do you get back to 100 percent?
faq.a: Find one percent or one part first, then scale up. 80 percent is 80 reais, so 1 percent is 1 real and 100 percent is 100 reais.
asks: How do I find the original price?

faq.q: Why is adding 20 percent back wrong?
faq.a: The 20 percent was taken from the original price, not the sale price. 20 percent of 80 is only 16, so adding it gives 96, which is too small.

faq.q: What is the quick way to do reverse percentages?
faq.a: Divide by the multiplier. After 20 percent off it is 0.8, so 80 divided by 0.8 is 100. After a 10 percent rise it is 1.1, so 110 divided by 1.1 is 100.

faq.q: How do you find a price before tax?
faq.a: Divide by the tax multiplier. A price of 220 rupees with 10 percent tax is 220 divided by 1.1, which is 200 rupees.
asks: How do I remove tax from a price?

facts: To undo a percentage change, divide by its multiplier.
Prices with tax included, such as VAT or GST, can be reversed this way to find the price before tax.

quiz.say: After a 25 percent discount, a game costs 60 dollars. What was the original price?
quiz.why: 60 dollars is 75 percent, so divide by 0.75 to get 80 dollars.

wrong.1: 75 adds 25 percent of 60, the wrong base.

quiz.say: A price with 10 percent tax is 220 rupees. What was it before tax?
quiz.why: 220 is 110 percent, so 220 divided by 1.1 is 200 rupees.

wrong.1: 198 takes 10 percent of 220 away, the wrong base.
wrong.2: 242 adds the tax a second time.
